card.architecture: Flux.2 rectified-flow DiT (Qwen3-8B encoder), 4-step distilled, whole-image img2img redraw
card.summary: Reinterpret an entire existing image through FLUX.2-Klein 9B using a prompt — the source is used as the init latent and re-sampled at a partial denoise with NO mask, so the composition is kept but the whole frame is redrawn in Klein's look at 4 steps. Higher quality than the 4B with best-in-family complex-prompt handling; non-commercial.
card.pick_when: You want a few-step FLUX.2 redraw with better quality than Klein 4B and don't need a commercial license.

prompt.guidance: Complex multi-clause prose is handled well by the Qwen3-8B encoder. Lower the redraw strength to stay close to the source composition; raise it to let Klein reinterpret more.
prompt.example: A bustling steampunk airship hangar with brass pipes and glowing dials, two engineers in leather aprons inspecting a propeller, dramatic volumetric light from high windows, intricate detail, cinematic wide shot
prompt.instructions:
Type the FULL description of the picture you want — this is a whole-frame re-render, not an edit instruction, and FLUX.2-Klein 9B follows natural-language prose.
4 steps, euler/simple, distilled guidance 4 (real CFG stays 1).
'Redraw strength' (denoise) controls how far the result drifts from the source: ~0.3-0.5 keeps the source's structure and mostly restyles it, ~0.7+ substantially reinvents it.
The source is sampled at its OWN resolution — no downscale, so the output keeps the input's size (FLUX-class models hold up to ~2K; a very large source is slow and can exhaust VRAM).
Negative prompts are inactive: the distilled weight runs at CFG 1.

ui_help.note: Send an image + a description; the whole frame is redrawn through FLUX.2-Klein 9B. 'Redraw strength' controls how far it drifts from the source.
ui_help.good_for: a few-step, higher-quality whole-image redraw keeping the composition

edit_use_cases: whole-image img2img: few-step redraw of an entire image through FLUX.2-Klein 9B, keeping composition
